research_spec.competing_explanation: Any ranking change could come from added parameter count or an extra regularization path rather than from modeling reusable user-specific exclusion structure. A width-matched additive-memory variant without subtractive scoring could explain the same effect if the proposed exclusion channel is not the true cause.
expected_evidence: A mechanism-off ablation that removes the subtractive exclusion term while preserving parameter count should materially reduce any advantage if exclusion memory is causal.
Qualification should show the exclusion-memory mechanism can be trained end-to-end under the frozen pairwise protocol and scored with full-sort NDCG@10.
User segments with denser mixed histories should be the most sensitive to the mechanism-off ablation if the exclusion channel is actually resolving conflicting evidence.
research_spec.falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if a matched-width control that keeps the extra memory parameters but uses them only as an additive preference channel matches or exceeds the proposed model, or if zeroing the exclusion score contribution at evaluation leaves ranking essentially unchanged.
research_spec.high_change_justification: The accepted context identifies a gap: prior fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off. This proposal is intentionally structured around a single removable scoring component—user-conditioned exclusion memory—so the core causal claim can be directly falsified rather than inferred from a bundled model change.
research_spec.hypothesis: To address the accepted gap around missing isolatable wedges and executable mechanism-off, a pairwise recommender with an explicit user-conditioned exclusion memory should be tested against a matched control and a mechanism-off ablation: if repeated pairwise mistakes on conflicting or niche interests create reusable negative preference structure, then subtracting an exclusion score from standard attraction scoring will improve full-sort NDCG@10; otherwise the effect should disappear under the mechanism-off test.
implementation_requirements: Add a matched control variant with identical embedding widths and gate computation but replace the subtractive exclusion term with an additive auxiliary channel so parameter count is preserved without exclusion semantics.
Add an executable mechanism-off evaluation mode that sets the exclusion contribution to zero after training while leaving all other learned parameters unchanged.
Construct the final score as attraction_score minus gated_exclusion_score, where the gate is computed from the user embedding and the positive-minus-negative contrast in the training triple.
Implement a BPR-style matrix factorization scorer with separate attraction embeddings and exclusion embeddings for users and items.
Report full-sort NDCG@10 overall and on user buckets defined only from training-history length or interaction diversity.
Train with standard pairwise BPR loss on the final score under train-only fitting.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use a parameter-matched BPR_MF descendant that retains the same extra memory tensors and gating network but routes the extra channel additively instead of subtractively, so the only tested wedge is explicit exclusion scoring.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Introduce a second user-item relation in BPR_MF: alongside standard affinity embeddings, learn exclusion embeddings that encode user-specific avoided directions. For each training triple (u, i+, i-), compute a gate from the user state and the contrast between i+ and i-, and use it to scale a subtractive exclusion score when ranking all items. The causal wedge is the subtractive exclusion pathway, which can be cleanly turned off after training.

research_spec.competing_explanation: Any gain could come merely from increased parameterization or history-attention smoothing rather than from the proposed explicit suppressor channel. A matched ablation that preserves the multi-slot encoder but removes the suppressor path is required to isolate the wedge demanded by the accepted context gap.
expected_evidence: Against a matched multi-slot attraction-only control, the full mechanism should improve full-sort NDCG@10 if explicit user-conditioned suppression helps disambiguate mixed-taste histories.

Removing only the suppressor contribution at evaluation time should reduce ranking quality more than removing an equal-sized amount of attraction-channel capacity, supporting the claimed mechanism-specific effect.

The learned suppressor weights should be non-trivial for a meaningful subset of users, especially those with diverse interaction neighborhoods, indicating the mechanism is actually used rather than bypassed.
research_spec.falsifier: If the suppressor-enabled model does not outperform the matched attraction-only control, or if suppressor activations collapse near zero/constant and the mechanism-off ablation leaves ranking unchanged, then the proposed structural wedge is not supported under this protocol.
research_spec.high_change_justification: This proposal addresses the accepted gap by introducing an explicit, isolatable mechanism-off wedge rather than another minor operator on an existing backbone. It changes the recommender’s core representation from single user/item embeddings to a small set of user preference slots plus a separate exclusion-memory pathway, and changes the core relation from pure attraction scoring to attraction-minus-suppression scoring. The mechanism can be cleanly disabled while retaining the same encoder family, making frontier qualification diagnostically sharper than prior resource-deferred variants.
research_spec.hypothesis: Because the accepted context identified a lack of an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off, a structural recommender that represents each user as a small mixture of latent preference slots and additionally learns a user-conditioned suppressor memory from pairwise contrasts will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over a matched attraction-only control under the frozen ML-1M protocol, by explicitly down-weighting candidate items that align with historical preference facets the user repeatedly rejects in hard pairwise comparisons.
implementation_requirements: For each pairwise training triple (u, i+, i-), form a suppressor update signal from the contrast between positive and negative item embeddings and aggregate it into a user-conditioned suppressor memory vector or small suppressor-slot set.

research_spec.mechanism_change: Introduce a dual-channel slot-based collaborative filter: an attraction channel routes each user-item score through a small set of user preference slots inferred from interaction history, while a suppressor channel learns a user-specific exclusion memory from positive-vs-negative pairwise contrasts and subtracts candidate evidence that matches historically opposed facets. The key executable wedge is the suppressor memory and subtractive gate, which can be turned off cleanly for matched comparison.

causal_chain: Adding a target-conditioned support scorer over the user's interacted items creates an explicit per-example notion of supporting evidence.
Earlier accepted context reports a diagnosis gap: fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off.
If this mechanism is real, support-aware removal should outperform a matched random-removal control with the same auxiliary loss budget; if not, gains reduce to generic regularization/noise.
Standard BPR-MF fits a static user vector, so any evidence about which specific history items support a positive target is only implicitly absorbed into that vector.

Training the model to preserve the positive-vs-negative margin after removing a high-support history item pressures the scorer to distribute support across multiple relevant history items instead of relying on a single brittle shortcut.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any observed gain would come from generic auxiliary regularization or stochastic history perturbation rather than from learning support-distributed user evidence for each positive target.
discriminative_predictions: A support-aware masking variant should beat an otherwise matched random-history-masking control at full-sort NDCG@10 under the same auxiliary weight and masking rate.
If the random-mask control matches the support-aware variant, the claimed support-distribution mechanism is falsified in favor of generic-noise regularization.
The support-aware variant should show smaller positive-score degradation under targeted support removal at evaluation-time probes than the parent and the random-mask control.
expected_evidence: Compared with BPR_MF, the new model changes score sensitivity patterns: positives depend less on any single historical interaction after training.
The mechanism-on vs mechanism-off comparison is executable with identical backbone, optimizer, and compute envelope.
Training remains within the protocol using pairwise triples and train-only user histories.
research_spec.falsifier: A matched mechanism-off that replaces support-aware removal with random history-item removal achieves indistinguishable or better NDCG@10 and similar robustness-to-removal probes, indicating the effect is not due to learned support distribution.
research_spec.high_change_justification: The proposal introduces a new target-conditioned history encoder plus a counterfactual stability objective defined on masked user histories. This cannot be reduced to parameter tuning or a thin wrapper around the parent objective.
research_spec.hypothesis: A BPR-trained recommender that augments static user embeddings with target-conditioned history support scoring and enforces pairwise margin stability under removal of high-support historical items will generalize better than plain BPR_MF and a matched random-mask control, because it suppresses brittle single-support shortcuts in user representations.
implementation_requirements: Add an auxiliary stability loss that penalizes collapse of the positive-minus-negative margin between full-context and masked-context scores.
Construct a masked context by removing one high-support history item from the weighted set.
Evaluate with full-sort NDCG@10 only on the frozen split.
For each training triple (u, i+, j-), compute support weights over the train-history items of user u using similarity between each history item embedding and the positive item embedding.
Form a history context vector as the weighted sum of user-history item embeddings and add it to the user representation during scoring.
Implement a BPR_MF descendant with item embeddings and a static user embedding backbone.
Implement a matched mechanism-off control that removes a random history item with the same masking frequency and auxiliary coefficient.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use the same backbone, optimizer, batch construction, auxiliary coefficient, and masking frequency, but replace support-aware history-item removal with uniformly random removal from the user's train history.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Add a target-conditioned support-distribution branch over user history and train for margin stability under support-aware counterfactual history removal.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: Disable the claimed mechanism by keeping the same auxiliary stability objective and masking schedule but selecting the removed history item uniformly at random instead of by learned support score.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: BPR_MF plus a positive-target-conditioned history context, with one additional auxiliary loss comparing full-context and masked-context pairwise margins; the sole discriminating switch is support-aware versus random history-item removal.
research_spec.observed_failure_mode: Accepted context identifies a research-process failure mode: earlier fresh realizations lacked an explicit isolatable wedge and executable mechanism-off, so this proposal centers a directly falsifiable on/off comparison.
research_spec.research_question: Does target-conditioned support-aware history masking improve full-sort ranking beyond what can be explained by generic masking regularization in pairwise collaborative filtering?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: The model is lightweight enough for the stated budget because it keeps the BPR_MF backbone and only adds per-example attention over a bounded user train-history sample plus one extra masked forward pass.

causal_chain: A disagreement-aware routing gate can upweight prototype-mediated evidence when direct affinity is uncertain and downweight it when direct affinity is already decisive.
A residual anti-collapse pairwise term prevents all interactions from collapsing onto the same dominant prototypes.
Representing each user and item as mixtures over a small shared prototype bank exposes multiple reusable intent/facet directions.
The resulting scorer should rank held-out items better than a matched single-channel collaborative filter under full-sort NDCG@10.
Users with mixed or ambiguous histories are poorly summarized by a single embedding.
research_spec.closest_parent: A recommender that represents each user and item as adaptive mixtures over multiple latent prototypes, then scores a pair through disagreement-aware prototype routing and a residual anti-collapse pairwise objective, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 by capturing multi-intent user preference and context-free item facet diversity that single-embedding pairwise matrix-factorization-style mechanisms cannot express.
research_spec.competing_explanation: Any observed gain would come only from increased parameter count or extra nonlinear scoring capacity rather than from prototype mixtures and disagreement-aware routing specifically.
discriminative_predictions: A parameter-matched single-embedding scorer without prototype routing should not reproduce the same concentration of gains on multi-interest users if the mechanism is genuine.

Relative improvement over the mechanism-off control should be larger for users whose histories are diverse or whose top direct-affinity scores are tightly clustered, because routing is only useful when direct evidence is ambiguous.

When the disagreement gate is disabled while keeping prototypes, ranking quality should move toward the direct-affinity control more than toward the full mechanism if adaptive routing is the active ingredient.
expected_evidence: Full model exceeds a matched direct-affinity control on full-sort NDCG@10 under the frozen split.
Per-user gain distribution is right-skewed toward users with broader interaction entropy or more weakly separated direct scores.
Prototype usage remains non-degenerate across training, indicating the anti-collapse term is functioning rather than letting one prototype dominate.
research_spec.falsifier: If a parameter-matched direct-affinity control or a prototypes-without-routing ablation matches or exceeds the full mechanism on full-sort NDCG@10, the claimed value of disagreement-aware prototype routing is not supported.
research_spec.high_change_justification: The parent mechanism is preserved semantically, but this proposal adds an explicit executable wedge, matched mechanism-off, and discriminative test structure that were previously unspecified.
research_spec.hypothesis: An executable pairwise recommender that scores user-item pairs by combining direct affinity with disagreement-aware interactions between user and item prototype mixtures, while regularizing against prototype collapse, will improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 over a matched single-embedding control because it can selectively express multi-intent preference structure that direct embeddings blur.
implementation_requirements: Compute user and item mixture weights over prototypes from their base embeddings using lightweight soft assignment layers.
Form a direct affinity score and a prototype-mediated score, then combine them with a scalar disagreement-aware gate derived from mismatch between the two evidence channels.
Implement trainable user base embeddings, item base embeddings, and a shared latent prototype bank in PyTorch.
Include ablations for mechanism-off direct affinity only and prototypes-without-adaptive-gate under matched training and evaluation settings.
Provide full-sort scoring for evaluation without using held-out data during fitting.
Train with a standard pairwise ranking loss plus a residual anti-collapse regularizer that penalizes degenerate prototype assignments or overly uniform routing.
research_spec.matched_control_requirement: Use the same dataset split, optimizer family, training loop, pairwise loss backbone, embedding dimension budget, and evaluation pipeline, but replace prototype mixtures and disagreement-aware routing with a single direct user-item affinity channel; keep total parameters approximately matched by widening the control embeddings if needed.
research_spec.mechanism_change: Instantiate the parent frontier hypothesis as a concrete two-channel scorer: direct user-item compatibility plus prototype-mediated compatibility combined by a disagreement-aware fusion gate, with an explicit anti-collapse regularizer on prototype usage.
research_spec.mechanism_off_definition: A matched pairwise collaborative filter that uses only one user embedding and one item embedding for direct affinity scoring, removing prototype mixtures, disagreement-aware routing, and the anti-collapse prototype regularizer.
research_spec.minimal_testable_wedge: Implement a static K-prototype mixture scorer with a scalar disagreement gate and compare it against a parameter-matched direct-affinity-only control on ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10.
research_spec.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise offline protocol, does an executable disagreement-aware prototype-mixture recommender outperform a matched single-embedding collaborative filter on full-sort NDCG@10?
research_spec.resource_hypothesis: A small-prototype implementation with lightweight gating is feasible within the qualification budget because training remains pairwise and scoring adds only low-order mixture operations on top of standard embedding lookup.
